To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of the trans-diboran complex 1 with chelating phosphines leads to cis-bisbaryl complexes 2,3.
the reaction of trans-bisboryldiboran(4)-platinum complexes with chelating diphosphines results in their transformation into the corresponding cis-bisborryl complexes.
the reaction of trans-dibora-4-ylplatinum complex with chelating bis(dicyclohexyphosphine) ligands results in cis-bisbora-4- ylplatinum complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new trans-diboran-4-yl platinum(II) complexes and the conversion of these compounds into their cis-biboryl analogues.

the synthesis of new cis-bisborene(2) complexes, which are rare in comparison with their trans analogues, as well as with the mechanistic understanding of the conversion of the diboran(4)-trans complexes into their cis isomers.
the preparation of cis-diboran(2)yl platinum complexes by oxidative addition of diborane(2) to a low-valent platinum center.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cis configuration of the chelating ligands in 2 and 4 induces the reductive elimination and subsequent oxidative addition of diborane(2) to the platinum centers, thus leading to the formation of the cis-bisboron(2) compounds.
the cis configuration of the two phosphines in the trans-diboran complex 1 forces a change in the site of oxidative addition of the diboranes(4), which is the first step of this transformation.
the trans configuration of the boryl ligands in 1 is retained in the reaction with the chiral bisphosphine ligand 4,5-bis(dicyclopentylphosphino)-9,9-dimethylxanthene (Xantphos).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diborane elimination from the trans-bisboryls 1 is induced by the cis configuration of the chelating phosphines, whereas the reductive elimination is favored by the presence of a trans configuration of the boryl ligands.
the trans-bisboryls can undergo a facile cis/trans isomerization, which allows for the preparation of the hitherto unknown cis-bisbora-n(4)yl complexes in a highly efficient manner.
the trans-bisboryls are the kinetically preferred complexes, whereas the cis-bis-boryls are the thermodynamically more stable ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trans-bisboryls 1 are not inert towards phosphine ligand exchange, and that the cis configuration of the ligands can induce the formation of cis-bisbories.
the diboran(4)-yl ligands in the trans-bisborylated complexes are readily displaced by phosphines.
the diboran(4)-trans-Pt(II) complexes are highly reactive and can be converted in situ into their cis-biboryl counterparts, which are more stable, isolable, and readily available.
